<subject>Re: Annelie Hettner</subject>
<body>
Klaus-Günter,  
If we consider it from a Hamburg grid index perspective, how would this appear? I believe he wants to float a price linked to the grid index but needs some sense of the typical basis to Hamburg we would apply. It’s not a firm offer since he’s unlikely to proceed with a transaction, so it’s more a market indicator. A bit unusual, but the more competitive our price is relative to Hamburg, the better our chances of securing the contract. We should present him with a solid offer, subject to credit approval and other conditions. When it comes to finalising the deal, he probably won’t commit given the units lack historical output data, so the market price could be quite different then.  

Arno  
</body>
<quoted>
 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Paffrath, Klaus-Günter  
Sent:	Wednesday, 18 June 2025 09:32
To:	Hertrampf, Arno
Cc:	Reising, Lorenzo; Johann, Fritz
Subject:	Annelie Hettner

Arno, here are the quarterly price indications for Annelie we discussed:

		Q3 2025			Q4 2025			Q1 2026			Q2 2026

Peak		120			65			50			49	

Off-Peak	57			38			30			28	

The prices shown are for firm capacity delivery with penalty clauses. Products contingent on generation output will be discounted 20%-30% on peak and 10%-20% on off-peak depending on contract duration.
